title: 8th European Political Community Summit Convenes in Yerevan — Canadian PM Joins for First Time
detail: Leaders from 47 European countries and beyond convened in Yerevan, Armenia for the 8th European Political Community (EPC) summit under the motto 'Building the Future: Unity and Stability in Europe.' The summit addressed democratic resilience, infrastructure connectivity, and energy security. In a historic first, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney attended as an observer — the first non-European leader to participate in an EPC gathering — reflecting transatlantic realignment driven by US isolationism under President Trump. Azerbaijan's President Aliyev participated virtually amid ongoing Armenia-Azerbaijan normalisation. The EPC format, which operates without binding written outcomes, served as an informal forum for heads of government from EU members and non-members, including UK Prime Minister and Balkan leaders. The next EPC summit was confirmed for Ireland in November 2026.

title: First-Ever EU-Armenia Bilateral Summit — Yerevan Marks Armenia's European Pivot
detail: On the margins of the EPC Summit, EU Council President António Costa and Commission President Ursula von der Leyen held the first-ever bilateral EU-Armenia Summit with Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan in Yerevan. The summit, confirmed in March 2026, reflected Armenia's strategic reorientation toward Europe following the 2020 and 2023 Nagorno-Karabakh conflicts and the withdrawal of Russian security guarantees. The joint statement covered connectivity (new transit corridors), energy (Armenian renewable exports to Europe), digital cooperation, and security assistance. The EU committed to an enhanced Comprehensive and Enhanced Partnership Agreement (CEPA) upgrade and increased financial support under the Global Gateway initiative. The summit marks the most concrete step yet in Armenia's post-CSTO European realignment.
